title: Invariants of Maximal S-Box Decompositions
summary: For decompositions of a bijection, maximality ensures irreducible S-box components; whether it forces equal component counts or size spectra remains open.

formal_statement.body: For a bijective function, consider any two maximal decompositions, where a decomposition is maximal when none of its individual S-boxes can be decomposed further. The unresolved question is whether the two maximal decompositions must contain the same number of S-boxes and, more strongly, must have the same size spectrum, meaning the same multiset of S-box sizes.

scope.domain: Structural questions about maximal S-box decompositions of bijective functions.
assumptions: Each decomposition is maximal: none of its individual S-boxes can be decomposed further.
parameters: S-box count: the number of components compared between decompositions
Size spectrum: the multiset of S-box sizes compared between decompositions
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether any two maximal decompositions of the same bijective function must have equal S-box counts and, more strongly, equal size spectra.

citations.label: Pitfalls and Shortcomings for Decompositions and Alignment

progress.summary: The paper defines maximal decompositions by non-refinability and explicitly leaves the component-count question open, along with the stronger size-spectrum question.
citation_labels: Baptiste Lambin et al., Pitfalls and Shortcomings for Decompositions and Alignment
